body:
1. What is Spring Boot?

Think of it as a 'Self-Driving Car' for Java. While traditional Spring requires you to manually shift gears and steer (XML/Config), Spring Boot handles the driving so you can just focus on the destination (Business Logic).

2. Spring vs. Spring Boot?

Spring is like a box of loose LEGOs; you have to find and connect everything yourself. Spring Boot is the pre-assembled LEGO Castle that you can customize if you want, but it's ready to play with immediately.
code:
// Spring: Needs DispatcherServlet, ViewResolver, and Context config manually.
// Spring Boot: Just add 'spring-boot-starter-web' and it's all done for you.

body:
3. What does @SpringBootApplication do?

It's a '3-in-1 Combo Meal.' It combines @Configuration (The Blueprint), @EnableAutoConfiguration (The Magic), and @ComponentScan (The Search Party) into one powerful stamp.

4. What are Starters?

They are 'Curated Playlists' for dependencies. Instead of picking 20 individual songs (libraries) for a party, you just play the 'Party Starter' playlist, and it includes everything you need.
code:
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
</dependency>

body:
5. How does Auto-configuration work?

It's like a Smart Thermostat. If it feels the room is cold (sees a Database driver in the classpath), it turns on the heater (creates a DataSource bean) automatically without you touching the dial.
code:
// Spring Boot checks @ConditionalOnClass and @ConditionalOnMissingBean 
// to decide whether to create a bean for you.

body:
6. What is Dependency Injection?

It's like a Restaurant Delivery. You (the Class) don't go to the kitchen to cook; you just sit at the table, and the waiter (Spring) brings the food (Object) to you when you need it.

7. @Component vs @Bean?

@Component is an 'Auto-Hire'; Spring finds the class and hires it. @Bean is a 'Special Contract'; you manually define how to create the object, usually for 3rd party libraries you didn't write.

8. What is the DispatcherServlet?

The Front Desk Clerk of a hotel. Every guest (Request) talks to them first, and the clerk decides which room (Controller) they should go to.
code:
// It's the core of Spring MVC architecture.
// It intercepts all HTTP requests and routes them.

body:
9. @RestController vs @Controller?

@Controller is a Librarian who hands you a physical book (HTML page). @RestController is a Digital Assistant who just sends you the raw text/data (JSON) directly via email.

10. How to handle Profiles?

Like different outfits for different weather. You have a 'Rainy' outfit (Dev DB) and a 'Sunny' outfit (Prod DB). You just tell Spring which 'weather' it is, and it switches the outfit.

11. What is Spring Actuator?

The Dashboard of your car. It shows you how much gas is left (Memory), how fast you're going (Traffic), and if the engine is overheating (Health check).
code:
// Just add the dependency and visit:
// /actuator/health or /actuator/metrics

body:
12. What is @Value?

It's a 'Sticky Note' on your fridge. Instead of hardcoding 'Milk' in your brain, you look at the note to see what the current value is, making it easy to change without 'reprogramming' yourself.
code:
@Value("${app.name}")
private String appName; // Pulls from application.properties

body:
13. Explain Spring Data JPA.

The Universal Remote for your TV. You don't need to know the complex wiring of the TV (SQL); you just press 'Channel Up' (save()) or 'Volume' (findById()) and it works.

14. What is @ControllerAdvice?

The Safety Net under a trapeze act. If any performer (Controller) falls (throws an Exception), the net catches them so the show (App) doesn't crash for the audience.

15. What are Embedded Servers?

It's like a 'Hot Pocket.' You don't need a separate oven (Tomcat installed on PC); the 'oven' is built into the food itself. Just heat it up (run the JAR) and eat!
code:
// Spring Boot JAR includes Tomcat/Jetty internally.
// java -jar myapp.jar

body:
16. What is @Qualifier?

The 'Pointy Finger.' If Spring sees two brothers (Beans) with the same name, it gets confused. @Qualifier lets you point and say, 'No, I want THAT one specifically!'

17. How to use @Transactional?

The 'All-or-Nothing' deal. If you're buying a house, you don't give the money unless you get the keys. If one part of the deal fails, @Transactional rewinds time like it never happened.

18. What is AOP?

The 'Background Music' in a movie. It plays throughout the film (App) without the actors (Business Logic) having to sing it themselves. It handles 'Atmosphere' like Security or Logging.
code:
@Around("execution(* service.*.*(..))")
public void logTime(ProceedingJoinPoint joinPoint) { ... }

19. What is Spring DevTools?

The 'Instant Refresh' button. Instead of restarting the whole engine every time you change a spark plug, DevTools detects the change and refreshes the app in a split second.
code: // Provides 'LiveReload' and 'Automatic Restart' during development.

20. Bean Scope: Singleton vs Prototype?

Singleton is a 'Public Park'; everyone shares the exact same one. Prototype is a 'Cup of Coffee'; every time someone asks for one, they get a brand new, fresh cup just for them.
